Paragraph:
Translation: For one who has taken his birth, death is certain; and for one who is dead, birth is certain. Therefore, in the unavoidable discharge of your duty, you should not lament.

Purport (Excerpt): One has to take birth according to one's activities of life. And, after finishing one term of activities, one has to die to take birth for the next... This cycle of birth and death does not, however, support unnecessary murder... But at the same time, violence and war are inevitable factors in human society for keeping law and order... By avoiding the discharge of his proper duty, he would not be able to stop the death of his relatives.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna is trying to prevent the inevitable (death of warriors) by abandoning his responsibility.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states the absolute certainty of the birth-death-rebirth cycle (Samsara). Because this cycle is unavoidable, neglecting one's prescribed duty to try and stop it is both futile and degrading.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is urged to face reality rather than hide from it. Death will happen regardless; the only variable he controls is whether he performs his duty righteously.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.locus of Control: Focusing on what can be controlled (action) vs. what cannot (death)
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.duty Over Emotion: Acting on principle rather than feeling

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Samsara (The continuous cycle of birth and death)
Karma (Action, which dictates the nature of the next birth)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The law of Karma ensures that death is merely a prerequisite for another birth. Since this cosmic mechanism is rigid and certain, mourning the natural transition is a waste of energy. Arjuna must focus on executing his Svadharma (duty as a warrior for justice) rather than trying to cheat the universe's design.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This verse addresses the 'illusion of control.' Arjuna thinks that by not fighting, he is saving lives. Krishna corrects his locus of control: death is certain regardless of Arjuna's choices. Psychological peace comes from recognizing what is outside our control (mortality) and taking responsibility for what is within our control (our immediate duty).
